aboutH2: Shifa Therapy: online counselling with Muslim therapists
intro: Shifa Therapy is an online counselling service that matches Muslim clients with Muslim therapists, psychologists and counsellors. Its Google listing gives an office address at 5800 Ambler Drive in Mississauga, but the therapy itself happens by video. There are no beds, no detox and no residential stays, so this is outpatient care you fit around work, school and family.

The service describes its work as faith-centred and grounded in evidence-based therapy. Therapists are expected to understand Islamic values, family expectations and the stigma many Muslims feel about asking for help. Clients pick a therapist by concern, language and gender, and the site says people of other faiths are welcome too.

pillars.title: Therapy that leaves room for your faith
pillars.body: Shifa Therapy's website points to a common problem: many Muslims put off counselling because they worry a therapist will judge their beliefs or tell them to set faith aside. Every therapist on the platform is Muslim and is expected to work with Islamic values, while still using methods with a research base behind them, such as CBT, ACT, EMDR, internal family systems and narrative therapy. You choose the therapist's gender and the language you talk in, which matters to a lot of families in Mississauga, Brampton and Scarborough.

pillars.title: Counselling for alcohol, drugs and gambling
pillars.body: Shifa Therapy has a dedicated page for addiction counselling, and therapists who list substance abuse and addiction as a specialty include an addiction counsellor with more than 16 years of experience who works with alcohol and drug use. Gambling addiction also appears in therapists' focus areas. The site talks openly about the shame and secrecy that often surround addiction in Muslim families. This is counselling only. There is no detox, medication or residential program, so people who need those usually combine this with a medical service.

pillars.title: Online sessions, booked on your schedule
pillars.body: Everything happens online. You answer three questions, look over the suggested therapists, pay by card and book a 50-minute video session, often in the evening or on a weekend. Prepaid packs cut the cost per session and do not expire, and you can switch therapists for free if the first match does not feel right. The Mississauga address on Google is an office; the website does not offer in-person visits, so call or message before you plan to go there.

overview: Addiction is one of the concerns it lists. Several therapists on the platform name substance abuse and addiction as a specialty, and gambling addiction appears among their focus areas. Sessions use talk therapy such as CBT and ACT. If you need medical withdrawal management or a live-in program, you would have to find that elsewhere and could use Shifa Therapy alongside it or afterwards.

Therapists work with adults, teens, children, couples and families, in English and languages that include Arabic, Urdu, Hindi, Bengali, Punjabi, Somali and Turkish. Beyond addiction, common reasons people book are anxiety, depression, trauma, grief, OCD, marriage problems, identity questions and the strain of Islamophobia or discrimination.

faqIntro: Answers come from Shifa Therapy's own website and public listings. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.q: Is Shifa Therapy a residential rehab?
faqs.a: No. Shifa Therapy is an online outpatient counselling service, and sessions take place by video from wherever you are. It has no beds, no detox and no overnight stays. If you need medically supervised withdrawal or a live-in program, look at residential centres in Mississauga, the GTA or elsewhere in Ontario, and consider Shifa Therapy for counselling alongside or after that care.

faqs.q: Does Shifa Therapy help with addiction?
faqs.a: Yes, it offers online addiction counselling with Muslim therapists. Several therapists on the platform list substance abuse and addiction as a specialty, including alcohol and drug use, and gambling addiction is among the focus areas they name. Counselling is talk therapy such as CBT and ACT; the service does not prescribe medication or manage withdrawal.

faqs.q: How much does Shifa Therapy cost?
faqs.a: A single 50-minute session costs US$80 to US$275, depending on the therapist's years of experience. Prepaid packs of 4, 8, 12 or 24 sessions lower the price, down to US$60 a session for the least experienced tier in a 24-session pack. Prices are in US dollars and are published on the Shifa Therapy pricing page, and the site says unused sessions do not expire.

faqs.q: Can I use OHIP or my work benefits?
faqs.a: OHIP does not cover these sessions, and Shifa Therapy does not bill any insurer directly. After you pay, it emails a detailed receipt that you can submit to your extended health benefits. Canadian plans usually reimburse only when the therapist holds a registration the plan recognises, so check with your insurer before you book.

faqs.q: Are the therapists registered in Ontario?
faqs.a: Not all of them. Shifa Therapy says its therapists are licensed in their home countries, and many practise from outside Canada. Some list Canadian credentials, such as a Canadian Certified Counsellor and Registered Psychotherapist (Qualifying), or a registered psychotherapist. Ask the team about a therapist's registration, or search the College of Registered Psychotherapists of Ontario register, before your first session.

faqs.q: What does faith-centred therapy mean at Shifa Therapy?
faqs.a: It means your therapist is Muslim and is expected to respect Islamic values while using standard, evidence-based methods. The site gives examples such as waswasa, halal boundaries and family expectations as things therapists understand from their own lives. You can choose a male or female therapist and a session language, and clients of other faiths are welcome.

faqs.q: How do I book a session?
faqs.a: You book online through the Shifa Therapy website. A three-question quiz about your concern, preferred therapist gender and language suggests matched therapists, then you choose one, pay by card and pick a time slot. Sessions last 50 minutes by video on a phone, tablet or laptop, and you can reschedule with at least 24 hours' notice. Support is available on WhatsApp at +1 226 828 9306 or by email at support@shifatherapy.com.

faqs.q: Can I switch therapists if it is not a good fit?
faqs.a: Yes. Shifa Therapy says you can change therapist at no cost, and its FAQ says it will help you find a better match and offer a complimentary 15-minute session. Refunds are available under the conditions in its refund policy.

Shifa Therapy's Google listing gives its address as 5800 Ambler Drive, Office 20, in Mississauga, Ontario (L4W 4J4). Its website describes the service as online only and does not mention in-person appointments, so contact the team before going to the office. Because sessions are by video, people use it from Toronto, Brampton, Oakville, Hamilton and across Canada.

Adults, teens, children, couples and families can all book. Therapists cover individual counselling, Muslim marriage and couples counselling, family counselling and child and adolescent therapy, in languages that include English, Arabic, Urdu, Hindi, Bengali, Punjabi, Somali and Turkish.

faqs.q: What if I am in crisis?
faqs.a: Shifa Therapy does not provide emergency care. If you or someone else is in danger, call 911. In Canada you can also call or text 9-8-8 at any time to reach the Suicide Crisis Helpline.
